name: Capel Sound
intro: Capel Sound runs along Port Phillip Bay west of Rosebud and east of Tootgarook. Its long beach, foreshore campsites and flat Bay Trail make walking and camping the main reasons to stop. Cafes and shops sit across Point Nepean Road from the reserve. Summer camping rules and availability change by season, so check the foreshore operator before making plans. The locality was renamed from Rosebud West in 2016.
factualLede: Capel Sound is a bayside town west of Rosebud, with a Port Phillip beach, foreshore campsites and a section of the Bay Trail.

tldr: Capel Sound is a bay-coast town between Rosebud and Tootgarook, with a long beach and foreshore camping.
Best for: a flat Bay Trail walk, beach time and a camping base close to the water.
Signature outing: follow the foreshore path toward Tootgarook, then return for a swim when conditions suit.
Allow a few hours for a walk and beach stop; check the operator for seasonal camping availability.
Rosebud and Rye offer further food stops along the bay.
notFor: visitors relying on guaranteed campsite availability
anyone expecting a dense restaurant strip
worstTime: summer holiday peak if you want an uncrowded beach
stayDuration: two nights minimum, a fortnight if camping
signature: A broad bay foreshore where camping and a flat coast walk set the pace.
skip: Assuming a campsite will be available without checking the operator's current booking instructions.
bestDay: Walk the Bay Trail toward Tootgarook in the morning, pause at the bay beach, then spend sunset along the foreshore.
insiderNote: Foreshore camping is seasonal. Check the operator's current booking instructions and cancellation waitlist before travelling.
heroDeck: A bay beach, foreshore camps and the Bay Trail on the doorstep.
